title: Design a gaming leaderboard.
description: Sorted score retrieval at scale: Redis sorted sets, rank-by-region sharding, tie handling, and fast top-N vs exact global rank.

data.text: **Question:** Design a leaderboard showing global and regional rankings and a player's rank around their own position.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Show top N players (top 100) with scores, updating near-real-time
Show 'my rank' — the player's position and neighbors around them
Support global and per-region leaderboards
Score updates arrive at high write rate (millions of games/day)
Handle ties deterministically (same score → earlier achievement ranks higher)

data.caption: Score events update Redis sorted sets; reads are served from Redis with periodic SQL snapshots
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Game servers] -->|score events| B[Score Service]
    B --> C[(Redis ZSET per board - global, region-US, ...)]
    B --> D[(SQL - score history, audit)]
    E[Read API - top N / around me] --> C
    C -->|periodic snapshot| F[(Object storage - board snapshots)]
    G[Rebuild job] --> C

data.text: The natural fit is the **Redis sorted set**: member = player id, score = leaderboard score. ZADD updates a player's score in O(log N), ZRANK finds rank, ZREVRANGE gets top N, ZRANGEBYSCORE/ZREVRANK gives neighbors for 'around me' — the whole feature is a handful of O(log N) operations on one data structure per board.

items: Composite member encoding for ties: store member as 'score:timestamp:playerId' inverted, or use a secondary rank index — pure score ties need deterministic ordering (earlier achievement wins)
One ZSET per board: global, per region, per season — sharding beyond a single ZSET happens by region/season, which is also the natural query dimension
'Around me' reads: ZRANK for position, then ZRANGE window of ±50 — one round trip after the rank; cache the window per session briefly
Write path: score events are idempotent (event id) and monotonic-max for lifetime boards (take max, not increment) — game servers may retry
Aggregation option: raw events stream via queue; an aggregator batches ZADDs to cut write amplification at 100k+/s
Durability: Redis is the serving layer, not the ledger — SQL keeps score history/audit; periodic snapshots let you rebuild a lost ZSET in minutes, not from nothing
Seasons/timetables: new board per season; top-N of last season migrated or archived; old boards TTL'd to cold storage
Scale beyond one Redis: region boards live near their players (global board is the aggregation problem — periodic merge of regional top-Ns, with exactness traded at the tail)
Anti-cheat: server-authoritative score events only; anomaly detection on implausible scores before they enter the board

data.title: Top-N is easy; global exact rank at millions is the design question
data.text: Top 100 from one ZSET is trivial. 'My exact rank among 50M players, globally, in real time' is the hard part — options: exact ZRANK while the ZSET fits in one shard; approximate rank (counting servers/HyperLogLog per score band) when it doesn't; or precomputed rank buckets. State which one you chose and what it costs.

rows: Serving structure in Redis; one per board
SQL ledger: history, audit, rebuild source

items: Tied scores at the top-100 boundary — deterministic tie-break, or the board flaps between requests
Redis restart — rebuild from SQL + snapshot; serve 'board temporarily estimated' state if recovery exceeds SLA
Score corrections (cheating rollback) — monotonic-max boards need an explicit set-down path with audit
Player changes region — global board membership follows; regional boards re-seat on next login
Season rollover spike — pre-provision the new ZSET; avoid live renames
Fan-out reads at reset moment (everyone opens the board) — CDN-cache top-N for seconds; 'around me' stays per-user

items.question: Why Redis ZSET and not SQL ORDER BY?
items.answer: SQL can do ORDER BY ... LIMIT for top-N, but per-read rank-of-me over millions of rows means OFFSET scans or dense-numbering jobs. A ZSET answers top-N, rank, and neighbor-window queries in O(log N) at read time with no batch renumbering.

items.question: How do ties work exactly?
items.answer: Encode ordering into the member or maintain a rank-index: equal scores resolve by earlier achievement timestamp, then player id — deterministic and stable across reads.

items.question: What if the board outgrows one Redis instance?
items.answer: Split by region/season first (natural shards). For one huge global board: approximate rank via per-band counters/HyperLogLog, or segmented sorted sets with rank-offset prefixes — exactness at the tail is where you spend engineering.

items.question: How do you rebuild after corruption?
items.answer: PlayerScore SQL table + last snapshot replay through the same idempotent update path; rebuild job verifies checksums (member counts, top-N diff) before cutting over.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Redis ZSET: ZADD/ZRANK/ZREVRANGE give O(log N) board, rank, and window reads
Tie-breaking must be deterministic; boards shard by region/season naturally
SQL ledger + snapshots make Redis loss a recovery, not a catastrophe
Exact global rank at massive scale is the real design problem — approximate deliberately
data.takeaway: Pick the data structure that answers all three questions (top-N, my rank, neighbors) natively — then engineer the rebuild path for when the fast layer forgets.
